checks.title: Post-#57 fork of a thread published by a client WITHOUT the partial grammar
checks.detail: [spec ambiguity — For Fable] blygger-studio's flattenFork consumes the `>` lines after every directive as part of it. For a pinned thread whose publisher predates the 2026-10-03 partial grammar (#49) those lines are the author's own blockquote — the bake shows a WHOLE quote — and the fork silently drops them, breaking §16.6f's "own prose copied byte-exact". The bake carries the answer (no `blyg-partial` class), so the fix is to consume the attached quote only when the baked element is partial. §16.6f should say which. | model: pass (10000 runs, seed 20261003, 174147 commands) | studio 0.20.2: fail (494 runs, seed 20261003, path 493:3:5:4:6:7:9:13:13:13:15:15, 9305 commands) — P6post: fork zz000000000000000000000009 of https://a.example/zz000000000000000000000003@v1: own prose line "> alpha" of the pinned content_md is missing from the fork

checks.title: Stub version agreement: stub_of.version equals the version baked of the same target
checks.detail: [studio bug (edge)] §10.6 rule 3 is about the stub's TARGET, an (origin, id) pair. blygger-studio's applyVersionAgreement matches baked quotes by id only, so a body quoting a DIFFERENT item that shares the id (own item vs. imported target) rewrites stub_of.version. Unreachable with random 128-bit ids (§5.1), reachable with copied or colliding ids; one-line fix (compare origin too). | model: pass (1000 runs, seed 20261003, 14980 commands) | studio 0.20.2: fail (936 runs, seed 20261003, path 935:8:7:13:14:12:11:11:11:11:13:15:15:18:18:18:18:18:21:23:25:25:25:25, 16203 commands) — P9: zz000000000000000000000008 v1: body does not quote https://b.example/zz000000000000000000000004, yet stub_of moved v2 → v1 (copied from a same-id quote of https://example.com/blyg/ — a different item)

checks.title: Importer differential (honest origins, faulty network)
checks.detail: [studio deviation (SHOULD)] §13.2: "Any suspected gap — the previously newest-seen entry no longer in the window — falls back to an index diff." blygger-studio reconciles on a gap only if some feed entry also triggered a fetch (`gap && triggeredAny`, poll.ts). A window in which the newest-seen entry vanished but every visible entry is already known (e.g. a truncated feed) leaves a newer version unfetched until the 24 h periodic index sync. The model follows the sentence; no loss is permanent. | model: not run | studio 0.20.2: fail (311 runs, seed 20261003, path 310:3:2:7:9:8:8:6:6:6:8:8, 4359 commands) — D1: importer state differs: https://b.example/ zz000000000000000000000003: model {"state":"current","version":2,"hash":"sha256:b63601e9443ce09003ffcf1d587fc83cc621fee05e68df6bd3c53b4d771002b8","retained":null,"hasContent":true} vs studio {"state":"current","version":1,"hash":"sha256:b63601e9443ce09003ffcf1d587fc83cc621fee05e68df6bd3c53b4d771002b8","retained":null,"hasContent":true}

checks.title: Thread publish outcome differential, spec-letter §10.2 step 1
checks.detail: [spec ambiguity — For Fable] §10.2 step 1 is "a local, currently-published item"; step 2 is "otherwise an imported item". Read literally, a local DRAFT or WITHDRAWN item with the same id falls through to the import. blygger-studio stops at any local row ("item is a draft" / "item is withdrawn"). Only reachable with id collisions, which §5.1 calls not a real case — but the order is normative text and the two readings differ. D2-shadow and D3 run under the studio's reading to look past it. | model: not run | studio 0.20.2: fail (311 runs, seed 20261003, path 310:9:14:15:7:7:7:7:7:10:10:10:12:15:15, 4856 commands) — D2: model accepted v1 — studio refused: item is a draft, not published
